warnings.title: Morning outlook
warnings.summary: NWS Norman expected severe storms late in the day, with the greatest tornado potential from 5 to 9 PM. The outlook described a front, dryline, strong instability and increasing wind shear.

warnings.title: First warning for central Canadian County
warnings.summary: Issued at 5:36 PM, this warning described a storm capable of producing a tornado near Hinton at 5:33 PM. El Reno was among the named locations.

warnings.title: Warning continued as the storm approached
warnings.summary: The 5:50 PM update described the storm near Calumet at 5:46 PM and continued the warning through 6:15 PM. This preceded the documented El Reno tornado formation.

warnings.title: A large tornado reported southwest of El Reno
warnings.summary: The 6:08 PM warning described a 6:05 PM observation six miles southwest of El Reno, moving southeast. Spotters and meteorologists were now tracking a large tornado.

warnings.title: The reported motion turns east
warnings.summary: Issued at 6:17 PM, the statement located the tornado northwest of Union City at 6:14 PM, moving east at 35 mph. These are operational estimates, separate from the later surveyed path.

warnings.title: The storm continues east of Union City
warnings.summary: The 6:24 PM update described a 6:19 PM observation northeast of Union City. It repeated the danger of a tornado obscured by rain.

warnings.title: Tornado emergency wording for communities farther east
warnings.summary: Issued at 6:28 PM, the new warning described the tornado southeast of El Reno at 6:23 PM. It named Yukon, Richland, Wiley Post Airport, Bethany and The Village in its tornado emergency wording.

comparison.title: The landscape before and after the storm
comparison.description: A matched regional view published by UW–Madison CIMSS shows the El Reno landscape on May 14 and June 2, 2013. Move the slider to compare the two observations. The red ellipse in the later image is part of the original source.
comparison.credit: Provided courtesy of Space Science and Engineering Center, University of Wisconsin-Madison. Terra MODIS imagery; comparison published by Scott Bachmeier. No ground photographer applies to satellite observations.
comparison.limits: 250-meter source resolution. This comparison shows landscape-scale change, not individual building damage. Different illumination, water glint, vegetation and image coverage also affect the appearance. The original publisher aligned these views; the museum has not performed a survey-grade registration. Browser framing and the original annotation are retained. Two source GIF frames were decoded to PNG without cropping or retouching. Noncommercial use under SSEC terms.

before.alt: Terra MODIS view of the El Reno and Oklahoma City landscape, May 14, 2013 · 17:01 UTC. Before the May 31 tornado.

after.alt: Terra MODIS view of the El Reno and Oklahoma City landscape, June 2, 2013 · 17:32 UTC. Red ellipse identifies the storm scar in the original source.

unmapped_fatalities.account: His published obituary identifies his death in El Reno on May 31. Contemporary reporting identifies him among the storm fatalities.
unmapped_fatalities.reason: The inspected obituary and named-fatality list do not establish a surveyed vehicle coordinate. No point has been assigned.

unmapped_fatalities.account: His obituary and contemporary reporting identify William O’Neal among those who died that day.
unmapped_fatalities.reason: A place name in a fatality list is not necessarily the location of the fatal impact. An independently supported incident coordinate remains unresolved.

unmapped_fatalities.account: Richard Charles Henderson, 35, was an amateur storm chaser from Hinton. His obituary records his name, age and death on May 31, 2013. National Geographic reports a recovery near a creek about a mile south of the TWISTEX wreck. That relative account does not establish where the fatal impact occurred.
unmapped_fatalities.reason: His identity and death are documented. Reports of recovery, road position and vehicle identity have not been reconciled into a named incident location. No precise pin is assigned.

sources.label: NWS assessment, section 3.9: four chaser fatalities

location_review.needed: To add a location, we need a public record or independently corroborated eyewitness account that names Henderson and distinguishes the impact site from the vehicle or body recovery site. A vehicle resemblance or an unnamed fatality symbol is not enough.

evidence.title: Identity confirmed
evidence.finding: His published obituary gives the full name Richard Charles Henderson, age 35, and his death on May 31, 2013.

evidence.title: Relative recovery account
evidence.finding: National Geographic places the recovery near a creek roughly a mile south of the TWISTEX wreck.
evidence.limit: A relative recovery description does not establish the fatal impact site or a unique coordinate.

evidence.title: Competing road and vehicle claims
evidence.finding: Stormtrack participants suggest Reno Road east of US 81 and, separately, SW 15th Street. They are discussing vehicles seen in footage.
evidence.limit: The thread does not verify which vehicle was Henderson's. These are research leads, not surveyed locations.

evidence.title: A correction within the discussion
evidence.finding: The final reply challenges the KFOR account cited earlier and links a contemporary survivor report.
evidence.limit: The linked NewsOK article could not be retrieved in this review. The challenge is recorded without treating it as a verified replacement location.

evidence.title: Official event account
evidence.finding: NWS records eight tornado deaths, all in vehicles, and describes several road areas.
evidence.limit: The event narrative does not pair Henderson's name with a precise location.

unmapped_fatalities.account: Juliana Keeping’s contemporary reporting places the family’s minivan on Interstate 40 at El Reno when the tornado struck. It names Maria Pol Martin and her son Rey Chicoj Pol.
unmapped_fatalities.reason: The account does not give a mile marker or coordinate. No particular point on the interstate is presented as their death site.

sources.label: Reporting by Juliana Keeping, republished by EMS World

log.title: Fatality records now include nearby survey photographs
log.finding: Opening the TWISTEX fatality record also shows photographs attached to nearby NWS survey points. Their source labels remain separate: a nearby photograph does not by itself identify a vehicle or its occupants. Henderson's record now explains the conflicting location leads and what evidence is still needed. No new fatality coordinate has been claimed.

log.title: All eight people remain visible beside the maps
log.finding: Richard Charles Henderson is identified as the amateur chaser from Hinton, with his obituary and the NWS assessment linked. Map controls now link the unresolved location accounts for all five people outside the TWISTEX recovery record. A completeness check prevents a named person from losing their location status. No precise location for Henderson is claimed.

log.title: Original dashcam moments on the shared clock
log.finding: Checked moments from Dan Robinson's original upload now select the historical map, radar and warning time. They remain discrete observations. Tim Marshall and Skip Talbot's legacy Vimeo players report unavailable; Robinson's former event webpage redirects to a closure notice. A successful HTTP request alone would miss these content failures.

log.title: Geography is now a separate reference layer
log.finding: USGS roads, towns and shaded relief can be shown beneath the historical observations. These are modern layers; they do not establish what a road or property looked like in 2013.

log.title: Warning issue time and observation time stay separate
log.finding: Seven preserved NWS products now accompany the shared clock. Future bulletins stay out of the current evidence display. Dashed polygons retain the coordinates printed in the original text and expire at the stated time. This is a curated sequence, not a complete warning archive.

log.title: An actual before-and-after pair
log.finding: Two frames from the original CIMSS satellite comparison are displayed with dates, source credit and limits. Ground photographs at different sites have not been passed off as a matched pair.

log.title: Five named people still have no defensible map point here
log.finding: The reviewed accounts support names and, in some cases, road or recovery context. They do not support precise named death-site coordinates. The remembrance list includes everyone while the map retains only the documented approximate TWISTEX vehicle recovery location.

log.title: The nearby vehicle photograph is not an identity record
log.finding: DAT record 165661 says Other and vehicle tossed. The preserved response does not name the vehicle or occupants. Its proximity to the TWISTEX recovery coordinate is shown as a research lead, not an identification.

log.title: Chaser footage may narrow vehicle movements
log.finding: A 2014 Stormtrack discussion compares vehicles at Highway 81, Reno Road and SW 15th Street, but also disputes camera timing and vehicle identities. A Reddit discussion points toward Randy Walton footage behind TWISTEX. These leads need original footage, clock alignment and independent identity checks before a named map location can be added. Neither complete video has been reviewed for this update.
